To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ease of making social judgments is influenced by both group variability and processing goal.
group variability and processing instructions have independent and interactive effects on the ease with which judgments are made about social groups.

(1) people find it easier to judge homogeneous groups than heterogeneous groups and (2) people find it relatively easy to judge groups when they have been instructed to attend to the differences between group members, regardless of the level of group variability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of variability in social categories on the ease with which judgments about these categories are made.
the effects of social group characteristics on the ease with which people make judgments about groups.
the effects of group homogeneity on the ease of forming judgments about a social group.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effects of group heterogeneity and homogeneity on the ease of forming an impression of a group are mediated by the effects of heterogeneity and homogeniety on the importance of the subordinate-level categories that are formed.
the effects of group homogeneity on judgmental processes are not uniform across all processing conditions.
the ease of judging a group depends on both the variability of the group and the processing set.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ease of making a judgment is influenced by the degree of variability in the social category and the type of judgment that is being made.

the ease of forming judgments about a group is a function of the extent to which group members are perceived to vary on the relevant dimensions, and the extent to which one's processing goals emphasize the similarities among group members or the differences among group members.
people find it harder to form impressions of heterogeneous groups, but easier to make judgments about the similarities and differences between group members, than homogeneous groups.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the consequences of group homogeneity or heterogeneity on social perception depend on the processing goal that the perceiver is pursuing.

group variability is a double-edged sword: it can be a source of difficulty when people are trying to form an impression about a social group, but it can also be a source of ease when people are trying understand the similarities and differences among group members.
group variability has a significant effect on the ease with which people can make judgments about a social group.
